messages:
jamie: Heads-up — ran the 2h replay harness this morning and saw a TTFT p95 jump around 40m into the run. Noticed kernel_selector switched to flash-attn-v2 for a subset of requests and latency rose.

sara: ugh. do we have a log of kernel selection events? could be fallback behavior under memory pressure.

jamie: yes, gist of the event stream is below. search for `kernel_selector: chosen=flash-attn-v2` in the runtime logs. also saw kvcache hit-rate dip from ~0.92 to 0.75 around the same time.

vik: can you paste the harness config? want to check batching mode + max_batch. sometimes latency-mode batching + aggressive coalescing changes TTFT drastically.

jamie: config excerpt:
```
batcher:
  mode: latency
  max_batch: 32
  coalesce_ms: 6
kernel_selector:
  prefer: [fp16, flash-attn-v2]
  fallback_order: [q4_0, q4_1]
```

marta: couple of quick hypotheses: 1) the replay workload had a few long-seq traces which broke KV locality -> colder KV cache -> higher token compute per request, forcing kernel change; 2) kernel-selector heuristics chose flash-attn-v2 for longer sequences which has different warmup/cold-start behavior.

sara: thanks. from a benchmarking methodology perspective, we should separate the variables: kernel selection, batching policy, and KV-cache warmup. apples-to-apples means pin the kernel and force identical batching across synthetic vs replay.

vik: agreed. proposed repro plan:
- pin kernel to the older `flash-attn-v1` and re-run replay harness
- run synthetic workload with matched seq-length distribution and same KV hit pattern
- capture NVTX traces + per-kernel micro-timings
- compute TTFT, TPOT, p95/p99, and goodput (tokens/sec that finished without fallback)

jamie: ran a quick pin test — results:
- baseline (pin v1): TPOT 420 tokens/s, TTFT p95 120ms
- replay (auto selector): TPOT 310 tokens/s, TTFT p95 210ms
- replay (pin v1): TPOT 400 tokens/s, TTFT p95 130ms
so most of the regression collapses when pinning the kernel.

marta: that implies kernel selection + KV behavior coupling. maybe selector uses a heuristic that mistakes KV miss cost and picks a kernel optimized for long sequence compute but not for short-turn latency.

sara: also remember to distinguish TTFT vs TPOT: TTFT is time-to-first-token (latency to start streaming), TPOT is time-per-output-token averaged over generation. For SLOs we often use p95/p99 of TTFT for latency but goodput (useful tokens / wall time) matters for cost.

vik: and QPS vs goodput: QPS measures requests/sec (useful for concurrency planning) but goodput ties to token throughput under real prompts. For apples-to-apples, match both request arrival pattern and per-request seq-length histogram.

perf-bot: perf-alert: regression detected on run 1769502460. Delta(TPOT) = -26% vs baseline. Ticket created: PERF-3221

jamie: created a short checklist to standardize comparisons:
1) warmup phase of 15 mins for KV cache and allocator stabilization
2) pin kernel when testing batching or when measuring kernel microperf
3) run synthetic with sampled seq-length and KV-hit profiles from production replay
4) record NVTX + kernel timestamps + selector decisions
5) compute TTFT p95/p99, TPOT median, goodput (tokens/s), and QPS
6) if selector differs between runs, rerun with forced-selection to isolate impact

marta: i'll own creating a small harness mode `compare-mode` that can pin kernels and replay KV-hit signals. will add to the loadtest repo.

sara: perfect. vik/ jamie — once we have micro traces, I'll triage whether the selector heuristic needs a tweak (prefer shorter-latency kernel for low-kv-hit scenarios).

vik: will run NVTX traces today and attach results to PERF-3221. thanks.

jamie: thanks all. let's keep this thread for quick status updates and link to the ticket for artifacts.
